stem: In contemporary rhetoric, the environment has been ____; we now speak of "natural resources" rather than "nature," as though the natural world were something to be sold, bought, or discarded.

(i)____ Kafka's halfhearted instruction that his unprinted manuscripts be destroyed after his death, his friend Max Brod set about publishing them immediately following the author's demise and thus became the (ii)____ Kafka's belated fame.

Some scientists speculate that changes in atmospheric methane were responsible for some abrupt global warming events in the past such as the one at the end of the geologic period known as the Younger Dryas. There is good evidence that large quantities of methane have been released quickly in the past through natural processes; however, methane is a relatively (i)____ molecule in the atmosphere and thus (ii)____ through chemical reactions with other compounds. The effect of even a large increase would therefore be (iii)____.
The overall persuasiveness of the literary critic’s analysis was occasionally marred by ____ generalizations that served only to distract attentive readers from the intended point.
It is not exactly socialism that has ____ so much of the country's economic life with cumbersome regulations but a meddlesome governmental culture that has been in place for centuries.
Many working physicists believe that general relativity, while ____, is itself only one aspect of a more comprehensive theory that embraces all the forces of nature.

Globalization has made ethnic entrepreneurship resilient in postindustrial economies: well represented in the small business sector in the United States, ethnic entrepreneurship has been ____ by the volatile tides of international migration.
